0.long_answer: Cystic hygromas are congenital lymphatic malformations that most commonly occur in the head and neck region, particularly in the posterior cervical triangle. In this area, the spinal accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI) courses superficially, making it vulnerable during surgical excision of the mass. Injury to this nerve can result in weakness of the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscles, leading to difficulties in shoulder elevation and head rotation. Thus, extra caution is required during the surgical management of cervical cystic hygromas to avoid damage to this nerve.
